q: How do I browse the full CSSBuy spreadsheet?
a: Open Browse finds from the homepage. The heading shows the current item range and total. Clear the category and search field to see the whole catalogue, then use the page-number box to jump directly to another page.

q: Why does my phone show fewer items than the page total?
a: A phone divides each catalogue page into smaller numbered ranges. Tap a range such as 21–40 to see the next group on that page. The page controls move to a different catalogue page.

q: How can I find a product if its seller title is hard to translate?
a: Start with a distinctive model number or brand plus one product word. Search again with a shorter phrase if the translated seller wording is too specific. A seller photo can give you another route to the listing.

q: What should I check when sorting by the lowest listed price?
a: Open the actual listing, select the colour and size you want, and compare its current price and availability. Record the selected variant before comparing a second listing. Two cards with the same photo can refer to different sellers.

q: What is the difference between a Weidian item ID and a SKU?
a: The item ID identifies the seller listing. A SKU identifies a particular combination of options within it. Matching the item ID gets you to the right page, but you still need to check the chosen colour, size or other option.

q: How do I copy the Weidian link for my chosen style?
a: Choose a style and complete any required size or other option. Once the selection resolves to one SKU, use the copy-style button. When reopening the link, confirm the selected options before ordering.

q: Why does a product have a seller link but no style picker?
a: The listing may expose a product page without a usable public option list. Open the original page to inspect its current choices. An item-level link by itself does not identify an exact colour or size.

q: How do I compare the same item across buying agents?
a: Open Other buying agents on the product detail page and choose an available destination. Match the seller item number first. Then compare the selected size, quantity and checkout estimate on each agent.

q: Does switching display currency change what CSSBuy charges?
a: The currency menu converts the spreadsheet price for comparison. Confirm the amount, settlement currency and payment-method charges in CSSBuy before paying. Exchange-rate changes can make a saved comparison differ from checkout.

q: What sort of image should I use for CSSBuy reverse image search?
a: Use a clear picture of one item, with the product filling most of the frame. A crop of the correct shoe or bag usually makes a better query than a screenshot containing menus, text and several unrelated items.

q: Can photo search match a colourway that is missing from the cover picture?
a: The index includes available style and gallery pictures as well as product covers. Upload the colourway you want, open a candidate and compare its actual option photos. Similar background colours can also produce a match.

q: Does a photo-search match prove that two products are identical?
a: A match indicates visual similarity. Compare distinctive details such as a pocket position, outsole pattern or buckle, then check the source item number and SKU. A high-ranked result can still be a different listing.

q: Which photos can I upload, and where is my query processed?
a: The search accepts JPG, PNG, WebP and GIF files up to 20 MB. Your browser compares the selected image against catalogue fingerprints. A newly added seller image becomes searchable after the relevant index refresh.

q: Which pictures are warehouse QC photos?
a: Look for the QC section on the detail page. A seller's studio picture or a variant thumbnail belongs to a different stage of the order. If the QC count is zero, examine the photos attached to your own warehouse order once available.

q: How does a CSSBuy Buy For Me order start?
a: Paste the seller link into CSSBuy, confirm the product, choose options and quantity, then review the order. CSSBuy purchases from the seller after you submit and pay. Keep the seller link with the order for later checks.

q: When should I choose CSSBuy Ship For Me instead?
a: Choose forwarding when you are purchasing from the seller yourself. Obtain the personalized warehouse address in your CSSBuy account and follow its inbound-parcel instructions. Keep the seller's domestic tracking number with your forwarding record.

q: What can I do if CSSBuy cannot read my product link?
a: Check that the URL opens the intended seller listing and copy it again from that page. CSSBuy directs users to Expert Buy when ordinary product search cannot retrieve an item. Include enough variant detail for the agent to identify it.

q: Can I buy a single unit from any 1688 listing through CSSBuy?
a: Check the supplier's minimum quantity and the price tier that applies to your intended quantity. CSSBuy's buying guide specifically flags supplier minimums on 1688. Recalculate the order if a low displayed price requires several units.

q: What order note helps prevent the wrong size or colour?
a: Use the exact seller option label, size and quantity. Add a concrete check, such as ‘Please confirm the size label reads 42.’ A seller item number and a specific observation are easier to act on than a broad request to check everything.

q: Which costs belong in a CSSBuy order budget?
a: Start with the selected item price and the seller's domestic delivery charge. Add applicable service costs and international freight. Keep any destination charges or optional services as separate entries until you know how they are billed.

q: Why are there two shipping charges for one purchase?
a: The first leg takes the purchase from the retailer to CSSBuy's warehouse in China. The second leg sends the packed parcel to you. When comparing sellers, keep the two legs in separate rows to avoid counting either one twice.

q: What information does the CSSBuy shipping calculator need?
a: Have the destination country, weight in grams, parcel dimensions in centimetres and relevant product attributes ready. Re-run the estimate using the packed parcel measurements when they become available.

q: Why do box dimensions matter if the item is light?
a: A large carton occupies more transport space than a compact one of the same weight. Enter its outside length, width and height in the route calculator. Keep the route and destination fixed when comparing packaging options.

q: Why do batteries or liquids change the shipping options?
a: The calculator asks for commodity attributes when finding available methods. Select the actual contents and read the eligibility conditions for each offered route. A method shown for ordinary clothing may be unavailable for a different parcel.

q: Should I consolidate all my warehouse items into one parcel?
a: Compare estimates for the combined package and for sensible smaller groups. Use the same destination and account for packed dimensions, fragile items and route restrictions. A larger carton or an incompatible item can change the comparison.

q: When should I request reinforced or vacuum packaging?
a: Ask about reinforcement for fragile contents and compression for suitable soft items. Consider whether retail boxes or garment shape matter to you. Obtain a revised estimate using the resulting dimensions before choosing a route.

q: How can I check a garment measurement in QC photos?
a: Identify the exact size and the measurement you need, such as a flat chest width from one underarm seam to the other. Compare it with a garment measured the same way. Ask about an unclear ruler position before sending the item internationally.

q: Why can the final international shipping charge change?
a: CSSBuy describes its initial shipping payment as a deposit. The packed parcel's verified weight and size influence the final calculation. Compare the final measurement and shipping method with the assumptions in your earlier estimate.

q: How long can an item stay in the CSSBuy warehouse?
a: CSSBuy's published FAQ gives 90 days of free storage from the In Warehouse status and describes a paid extension. Check the date and extension terms on your own order before waiting for another item to arrive.

q: What should I check before requesting a CSSBuy return?
a: Contact CSSBuy promptly while the item is in the warehouse. Its FAQ lists seller acceptance, a warehouse stay under seven days and payment of return shipping among the conditions. Check the conditions for the specific order before treating a return as approved.

q: Where can I track a CSSBuy parcel after dispatch?
a: Open My Parcel in your CSSBuy account and select the international parcel. Use the parcel reference when asking about that shipment. Keep the seller's domestic tracking separately, as it follows the earlier journey to the warehouse.

q: What evidence should I keep if an item arrives damaged?
a: Photograph the outer packaging, protective materials and affected area before discarding them. Keep the parcel number, item number and a short description of the issue. CSSBuy's after-sales help asks for pictures of both the goods and the packaging.
